summary: Customer C00348 alerted the bank to unauthorized activity on card C00348-K1 regarding transaction 3660250 ($4.05). Graph investigation revealed a 6-transaction run of low-value online product C authorizations between January 7 and January 28, 2017, totaling $23.17, which is completely unprecedented against the cardholder's historical baseline of in-person product W purchases. Crucially, scheme peer analysis identified 19 other cards across 19 customers exhibiting identical micro-billing patterns with contiguous transaction IDs in the 3660xxx block, reflecting coordinated batch processing. Based on the customer dispute and decisive cross-card evidence, the activity was confirmed fraudulent and classified as an undocumented scheme under Rule R9. The card was blocked, peer cards were flagged for monitoring, and a suspicious activity report was initiated.
open_question: While the sequential micro-transactions clearly form part of an escalating multi-card scheme across 19 peers, the exact merchant identity, merchant category, and technical vector used to initiate the recurring online product C charges remain unrecorded due to missing device fingerprints and absent merchant descriptor details.
